notes.summary: HCF is the biggest number that divides given numbers; LCM is the smallest number they all divide. SSC asks 0 to 1 question in each tier, often as a remainder or "together again" word problem. Decide first whether the question wants the HCF or the LCM; the rest is quick.

concepts.title: What HCF and LCM mean
concepts.body:
A factor of a number divides it exactly: factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. A multiple is the number times 1, 2, 3, ...: multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, ...

HCF (highest common factor, also called GCD) is the biggest number that divides all the given numbers. LCM (least common multiple) is the smallest number that all the given numbers divide.

The HCF always divides the LCM. The HCF is never bigger than the smallest number; the LCM is never smaller than the biggest number. If two numbers are co-prime (HCF 1), their LCM is their product.

concepts.title: Prime factor method
concepts.body:
Write each number as a product of prime powers.

  • HCF = common primes, each with its lowest power.
  • LCM = all primes that appear, each with its highest power.

Example: 12 = 22 × 3, 18 = 2 × 32, 30 = 2 × 3 × 5.
HCF = 2 × 3 = 6. LCM = 22 × 32 × 5 = 180.

The same works when the numbers are given in power form, such as 23 × 92 × 13. First turn 92 into 34 so that every base is prime.

concepts.title: Division method for big numbers
concepts.body:
For two large numbers, divide the larger by the smaller, then divide the last divisor by the remainder, and repeat. The last non-zero divisor is the HCF. In short, HCF(a, b) = HCF(b, remainder of a ÷ b).

Example: HCF of 1071 and 462.
1071 = 2 × 462 + 147
462 = 3 × 147 + 21
147 = 7 × 21 + 0
HCF = 21.

For three numbers, find the HCF of two, then the HCF of that answer with the third. LCM can be built the same way: LCM(a, b, c) = LCM(LCM(a, b), c).

Useful fact: HCF(a, b) also divides a − b and a + b.

concepts.title: HCF × LCM = product of two numbers
concepts.body:
For two numbers a and b: HCF × LCM = a × b.

Example: HCF 12, LCM 924, one number 84. Other number = 12 × 924 ÷ 84 = 132.

This rule does not hold for three or more numbers. For example 2, 4, 6 have HCF 2 and LCM 12, so HCF × LCM = 24, but the product is 48.

Check for impossible data: the LCM must be a multiple of the HCF. HCF 8 with LCM 60 cannot happen.

concepts.title: Numbers in a ratio, and counting pairs
concepts.body:
If the HCF of two numbers is h, the numbers are h × a and h × b, where a and b are co-prime. Then LCM = h × a × b.

Example: numbers in the ratio 3 : 4 with LCM 180. Numbers are 3h and 4h; LCM = 12h = 180, so h = 15 and the numbers are 45 and 60.

Counting pairs. Product 1500, HCF 10. Then h2 × a × b = 1500, so a × b = 15. Co-prime pairs with product 15: (1, 15) and (3, 5). So 2 pairs: (10, 150) and (30, 50).

With a sum: HCF 12, sum 96. Then 12(a + b) = 96, a + b = 8. Co-prime pairs: (1, 7) and (3, 5). Numbers (12, 84) and (36, 60). The pair (2, 6) is not allowed because 2 and 6 are not co-prime.

concepts.title: HCF and LCM of fractions and decimals
concepts.body:
Write each fraction in its lowest terms first.

  • HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators
  • LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators

Example: 2/3, 4/9, 5/6. HCF = HCF(2, 4, 5)/LCM(3, 9, 6) = 1/18. LCM = LCM(2, 4, 5)/HCF(3, 9, 6) = 20/3.

Decimals: make the number of decimal places equal, remove the point, find the HCF or LCM, then put back the same number of decimal places.
Example: HCF of 0.6, 0.9 and 1.5: think of 6, 9, 15, HCF 3, so the answer is 0.3.

concepts.title: Greatest number that divides with remainders (HCF type)
concepts.body:
ConditionAnswer
Divides a, b, c exactlyHCF(a, b, c)
Leaves the same given remainder rHCF(a − r, b − r, c − r)
Leaves remainders r1, r2, r3HCF(a − r1, b − r2, c − r3)
Leaves the same remainder, not givenHCF of the differences: HCF(b − a, c − b, c − a)

The answer must be larger than every remainder, so check it.

Example: greatest number dividing 43, 91 and 183 with the same remainder. Differences 48, 92, 140. HCF = 4.

concepts.title: Least number that leaves remainders (LCM type)
concepts.body:
ConditionAnswer
Divisible by a, b, cLCM(a, b, c)
Leaves the same remainder r each timeLCM + r (in general, k × LCM + r)
Remainders fall short of each divisor by the same amount k (for example 5 leaves 3, 6 leaves 4: short by 2)LCM − k

If the number must also be divisible by another number m, try k = 1, 2, 3, ... in k × LCM + r until it divides by m.

Example: least number which leaves 8 when divided by 12, 15, 20 and 54. LCM = 540, so 540 + 8 = 548.

Greatest n-digit number divisible by a, b, c: take L = LCM, then 999...9 minus its remainder on division by L. Smallest n-digit: 100...0 plus (L − remainder).

concepts.title: Things happening together (LCM)
concepts.body:
When events repeat every a, b and c units of time, they happen together again after LCM(a, b, c).

Example: bells toll every 6, 8 and 12 minutes and toll together at 9:00 a.m. LCM = 24 minutes, so next at 9:24 a.m.

How many times together in a period T (counting the start) = [T ÷ LCM] + 1.
Runners on a circular track meet at the starting point after the LCM of their lap times.

Keep units the same: change hours to minutes or minutes to seconds before taking the LCM.

concepts.title: Largest equal pieces and fewest tiles (HCF)
concepts.body:
When things must be cut, packed, or measured into the largest equal parts with nothing left over, use the HCF.

  • Largest measuring jar for 403 L, 434 L and 465 L of milk: HCF = 31 L.
  • Least number of square tiles for a floor = floor area ÷ (side of tile)2, where the tile side = HCF of length and breadth.
  • Least number of rows with equal students of one kind each = total ÷ HCF.

Example: a floor 6 m 24 cm by 4 m 32 cm. HCF(624, 432) = 48 cm. Tiles = (624 ÷ 48) × (432 ÷ 48) = 13 × 9 = 117.

Quick test: "largest", "maximum size", "greatest length" suggests HCF; "least time", "next together", "smallest number of" (of a common multiple) suggests LCM.

concepts.title: HCF and LCM of algebraic expressions
concepts.body:
Factorise each expression fully, then treat the factors like primes: HCF takes common factors with the lowest powers, LCM takes all factors with the highest powers.

Example: x2 − 8x + 15 = (x − 3)(x − 5) and x2 − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3).
HCF = (x − 3). LCM = (x − 2)(x − 3)(x − 5).

The product rule also holds for two expressions: HCF × LCM = product of the two expressions (up to a constant sign).

varieties.name: Find the HCF or LCM
varieties.how: Factorise each number into primes. HCF: common primes with lowest powers. LCM: every prime with its highest power.

example.q: Find the HCF and LCM of 72, 108 and 180.

varieties.name: HCF × LCM = product
varieties.how: For two numbers only: other number = HCF × LCM ÷ given number.

example.q: The HCF of two numbers is 16 and their LCM is 384. One number is 128. Find the other.

varieties.name: Numbers from ratio, sum or pairs
varieties.how: Write the numbers as h × a and h × b with a, b co-prime. Then LCM = h × a × b. Use the given sum, product or LCM to find h, or to list the co-prime pairs.

example.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their LCM is 180. Find the numbers.
steps: Let the numbers be 3h and 4h; 3 and 4 are co-prime.

varieties.name: HCF and LCM of fractions and decimals
varieties.how: HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators. LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators. For decimals, equalise decimal places first.

varieties.name: Greatest number that divides with remainders
varieties.how: Subtract each remainder from its number and take the HCF. If the remainder is the same but not given, take the HCF of the differences between the numbers.

example.q: Find the greatest number that divides 43, 91 and 183 leaving the same remainder in each case.
steps: Check: each number leaves remainder 3 on division by 4.

varieties.name: Least number that leaves remainders
varieties.how: Find the LCM. Same remainder r: answer is k × LCM + r. Fixed shortfall k: answer is LCM − k. If it must also divide by another number, try k = 1, 2, 3, ...

example.q: Find the least number which leaves remainder 2 when divided by 6, 9, 15 and 18, but is exactly divisible by 7.

varieties.name: Bells, lights and runners together
varieties.how: Bring all intervals to the same unit and take their LCM. Add the LCM to the starting time.

example.q: Three runners complete one lap of a track in 30 s, 45 s and 60 s. They start together from the same point. After how long will they next be together at the start?

varieties.name: Largest equal pieces and fewest tiles
varieties.how: Convert to the same small unit. The largest equal piece is the HCF. Number of pieces or tiles = total ÷ piece (for tiles: area ÷ side<sup>2</sup>).

example.q: A floor is 6 m 24 cm long and 4 m 32 cm wide. Find the least number of equal square tiles that will cover it exactly.

varieties.name: HCF and LCM of algebraic expressions
varieties.how: Factorise each expression. HCF: common factors. LCM: every factor once, with its highest power.

example.q: Find the LCM of x<sup>2</sup> − 8x + 15 and x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 6.

tips: Words like "greatest", "largest size" or "maximum length" point to HCF; "least", "next together" or "smallest number divisible" point to LCM.
HCF × LCM = product works only for two numbers.
In option questions, the LCM must be a multiple of the HCF; strike out options that break this.
For "same remainder, not given", take the HCF of the differences between the numbers.
For a fixed shortfall (divisor − remainder is the same each time), the answer is LCM − shortfall.
Convert all lengths or times to one unit before finding HCF or LCM.
traps: Reduce fractions to lowest terms before finding their HCF or LCM.
When counting pairs from a given HCF, the two multipliers must be co-prime.
In bell questions, adding the LCM to a clock time can cross the hour; count minutes carefully.
The greatest divisor must be larger than every remainder; check it.

formulas.name: Two numbers
formulas.expr: HCF × LCM = first number × second number

formulas.name: Numbers with HCF h
formulas.expr: ha and hb (a, b co-prime), LCM = hab

formulas.name: HCF of fractions
formulas.expr: HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators

formulas.name: LCM of fractions
formulas.expr: LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators

formulas.name: Greatest divisor leaving remainders r₁, r₂, r₃
formulas.expr: HCF(a − r₁, b − r₂, c − r₃)

formulas.name: Greatest divisor leaving the same remainder
formulas.expr: HCF(b − a, c − b, c − a)

questions.q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 924 respectively. If one of the numbers is 84, the other number is:
What is the LCM of 12, 18 and 30?
Find the greatest number that divides 1305, 4665 and 6905 leaving the same remainder in each case.
Three bells toll at intervals of 6, 8 and 12 minutes. If they toll together at 9:00 a.m., when will they next toll together?
questions.solution:
They toll together after LCM(6, 8, 12) minutes.
LCM = 24 minutes.
9:00 a.m. + 24 min = 9:24 a.m.

questions.q: What is the least number which, when divided by 12, 15, 20 and 54, leaves a remainder of 8 in each case?
What is the HCF of 2/3, 8/9 and 16/81?
questions.solution:
HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators.
HCF(2, 8, 16) = 2; LCM(3, 9, 81) = 81.
HCF = 2/81.
